one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent chose a fragile regex-based sanitization strategy at step 3, missing critical attack vectors (iframe/object/embed tags, generic on* attributes, javascript: in non-href/src attributes) and producing malformed HTML remnants, while its self-crafted tests never exposed these deficiencies.
t_err_evidence: I should use string manipulation rather than HTML parsing libraries
t_commit_evidence: Once filter.py was written with the regex approach at step 3, all subsequent steps only refined regex details or ran self-written tests; the agent never reconsidered using a DOM parser (e.g., BeautifulSoup), so the failing strategy was permanently committed at step 3.
trigger_explanation: The agent acted on the unverified assumption that string-level regex substitution is sufficient to safely sanitize HTML while preserving formatting, without checking what attack vectors the task actually requires to be handled or whether an existing library is specified. This false premise led directly to choosing a regex approach that is both incomplete (misses vectors) and over-aggressive (strips entire href/src attributes).
